A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMCEE framework. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations, component ablations, model comparisons and qualitative analyses, including additional experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds stronger-model comparisons, retrieval and merging controls, repeated-run results and a human evaluation.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains synthetic-context extraction, an English CoT reasoning response, and judgment-based merging. New alternative combinations are experimental comparators, not changes to the adopted EMCEE pipeline.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds a focused human assessment of generated-context quality on 51 Korean GlobalOpinionQA items. Existing benchmark, language and country coverage is retained; GlobalOpinionQA and Aya evaluations already appeared in v2's appendices.

E2.justification: v3 adds multiple alternative response-merging pipelines in Table 23, full-passage and multi-passage RAG variants including dense reranking in Table 24, and an EXTRACT-plus-EXTRACT merging comparator labeled RECITE in Table 25. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison methods; Table 1's comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-5 and Claude-4-Sonnet evaluation on 100 M3-Exam questions per language, expanded retrieval configurations on similarly sized subsets, and additional full-M3-Exam merging controls. The human study introduces five bilingual Korean raters evaluating 51 English-presented items on four five-point scales. The original main-benchmark protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Appendices B.5-B.8 add exemplar-selection robustness, alternative merging combinations, retrieval-strength controls and a context-only recitation-style comparison. Appendix D directly assesses synthetic-context quality, while Table 19 supplies numerical evidence for the previously described language-cue ablation. The relocated MKQA failure example is retained evidence, not a new case study.

E5.justification: Unlike v2's point estimates, B.5 reports three independent seeds with resampled few-shot exemplars and mean plus standard deviation for four methods. Table 26 also reports variability in human ratings. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting without establishing a specific increase over any previously documented run count.

E6.justification: New results include GPT-5 accuracy of 76.0 for EMCEE versus 74.3 for NATIVE-BASIC, and Claude-4-Sonnet accuracy of 82.3 tying XLT, alongside new control and human-evaluation outcomes. Table 3 corrects Llama EMCEE from 57.6 to 56.9, matching v2's appendix. Figure 4 also changes language-level scores and reverses EMCEE's lead over ENG-COT in Thai, despite unchanged Table 1 aggregates and no explained setting revision.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs for EMCEE. The conceptual method description is retained, and the new empirical rating criteria do not introduce mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: extracting internal multilingual knowledge and combining it with reasoning through a judge. The headline relative improvements of 16.4% overall and 31.7% for low-resource languages are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 corrects the Aya interpretation from outperformance across all four languages to average gains with an Italian exception, consistent with the unchanged scores. It adds interpretations concerning seed stability and human-rated cultural quality, factuality and safety, while acknowledging the human study's limited language and sample coverage. The MKQA failure interpretation already existed in v2.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link on page 1 and documents passage-count and truncation configurations for the extended RAG comparisons. Core prompt templates, exemplar-construction instructions and original decoding details are retained. Detailed identification of the new reranker is not supplied.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Appendix B.8 explicitly positions EMCEE against a recitation-inspired, context-only comparator. Section 4 condenses the earlier MGSM and synthetic-supervision discussion. These are limited refinements of positioning rather than a substantial expansion of related work.

P1.justification: GlobalOpinionQA, Aya and the MKQA failure discussion move from appendices into the main text. Related work is shortened, some appendix explanations are rewritten, and title capitalization, author presentation and acknowledgments are updated. The overarching narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven result tables, redraws the language-wise plots with revised colors, and reorders the XNLI language display. It moves existing GlobalOpinionQA and Aya tables into the main text, compresses and relocates the MKQA failure figure, and relocates the detailed cross-model table. These substantially reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Stronger retrieval and merging controls, first seed-variability results and direct human assessment improve the evidential basis beyond v2's point estimates and narrow retrieval baseline. Correcting the Aya interpretation and Llama summary value also improves accuracy. The net benefit is limited by the small human study, incomplete new implementation details and unexplained Figure 4 revisions that conflict with the retained Table 1 aggregates.
